claims.text: Gallego-Blanco’s study dates the Fourth Council of Toledo to December 633 under Sisenand and Isidore. Canon 75 prescribed royal succession by nobles and bishops and public judgment with leading men, excluding a popular assembly; the study distinguishes this rule from usurpation in practice.

claims.text: Gallego-Blanco distinguishes Toledo’s elite succession prescription from armed usurpation in practice. Cordoba’s account instead names a governor choosing a capital and later an independent Umayyad court, with separately situated repairs. A council rule, an appointment and a court are different relationships. These two city witnesses neither establish identical government throughout Iberia nor prove popular acceptance. The original instruments remain uncollated; the rule cannot be substituted for what actually happened.
